note: For each position i define a_i as the largest length of an increasing subsequence ending at x_i and b_i similarly for decreasing. Under failure of the desired conclusion, 1<=a_i,b_i<=n. For i<j, distinctness gives x_i<x_j or x_i>x_j. In the first case append x_j to a longest increasing subsequence ending at i, obtaining a_j>=a_i+1; in the second obtain b_j>=b_i+1. Hence all ordered pairs (a_i,b_i) are distinct, impossible for n^2+1 indices and only n^2 pairs in {1,...,n}^2. This proves the complete theorem without external facts.
